_comment: CLAIM fracture::6: [Numerical] Seeding a pre-crack by writing a large value into the history field makes the damage overshoot one slightly near the seed, which is harmless but will trip a naive assertion that d <= 1. Signal: max(d) comes out a fraction of a percent above one from the very first load step, at nodes on the boundary between seeded and unseeded cells; it is the AT2 gradient term smoothing a step change in the driving force, not a solver failure. Check min(d) >= 0 and that the regularised surface energy increases, rather than asserting a hard upper bound of one. The same overshoot region is where the small non-monotone decreases of d appear even with the history field enabled. WHAT THIS RUNS: a staggered AT2 phase-field solve on a 20x20 unit square, P1 displacement and P1 damage, E=210, nu=0.3, Gc=2.7e-3, l0=2h=0.1, pre-crack along y=0.5 for x<0.5 seeded as a large history value, three displacement-controlled load steps with the history maximum enabled; the mutant seeds the identical pre-crack with a Dirichlet condition d=1 on the notch nodes instead. WHAT WAS PRINTED: the damage subproblem is linear and unconstrained, so max(d) reads 1.0187 immediately after seeding - 1.87% over the bound - and stays above one at every load step (1.0178, 1.0152, 1.0101); the argmax node sits at (0.4500, 0.5000), the tip of the seeded band; min(d) stays non-negative (1.2e-03 to 2.1e-02) and the regularised surface energy rises 2.18e-03 -> 2.30e-03 -> 2.80e-03. A naive `assert d.x.array.max() <= 1.0` raises AssertionError. The worst non-monotone nodal decrease during loading, -0.00506, occurs at the same node (0.4500, 0.5000), which is the claim's last sentence. Dirichlet seeding gives max(d) = 1.0 exactly. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 on dolfinx 0.10.0 / basix 0.10.0 (conda env `fenics`, real scalars); every expect_in_output string was copied from that run. T2_MUTATE=1 seeds the pre-crack with a Dirichlet condition and the fixture then fails its own expectations.
